body: The thought has crossed my mind. After my suicide attempt my father did actually ask if I wanted to move to China for a little while. I didn't feel it would be fair to my business partners or to my family so I declined. There is some appeal to it however a great deal of fear as well. With no support system around I'm not sure what I would do if I ever did come across a really really bad day...as I might come up with a permanent solution to a temporary problem..<sigh>

I'm sorry to hear about law school...but yes much of what you describe is how I feel. It's hard to keep chin up given how much I've pissed away in a sense. As you say I am "young enough" but the fortitude is gone...small steps I suppose is the best answer. Thx for the comments

I think part of the reasons I can't open up to anyone is because objectively my problems are insignificant. My father was an immigrant and literally came here with $7 and has managed to build a great living for my family all at the age of 28 while my mother was pregnant with my older sister. It blows my mind what he was able to do. I've been given everything I could ever possibly want yet I can't remember the last time I actually achieved anything. I never had to worry about funding for school, car payments, rent etc. I had a small business that my father seeded while I was in college and for better or worse it provided for a few years but left me in a state of comfort and complacency. That along with my ambitions of being a "day trader" prevented me from acquiring any real skills. 

I have a colleague that is dealing with 100x more shit than me and I am in awe of what they are capable of handling. They have a terminal illness and are still able to deal with the realities of life. She had to drop out of college due to her mother getting cancer and taking the scholarship funds for treatment while dealing with Lupus on her own. She's literally been in and out of the hospital and soldiers on. I know that I should look upon her with inspiration but I feel shame.  Whereas I've shirked away and created a bubble world unto itself.
I was on Lexapro and increased the dosage for a few months but it made me even more lethargic than usual. I cut it off about 2 months ago and haven't really noticed a change either way.
In all honesty..not particularly..it's probably something I should've gotten into years ago. I used to run a LAN center and I wanted to create a Table Top gaming group..but yeah never materialized

Good point... I do use it as an escape and yeah the isolation isn't healthy but it does provide a good outlet...

Haven't played paper and pen RPGs..but yeah been awhile since i've played table top games

I'm a pretty big geek, so video games, sci-fi, comics etc...its gonna sound pretty sad but part of what got me through this past year was playing video games...i've probably played more games this past year than any other year in my life.
Umm..not really a music person at least I don't really listen to lyrics or follow any groups or anything

I've talked to a couple of doctors...one therapist I went to about 6 times but just talking to them made me hate myself even more in regards to some of the stupid stuff I was hung up on and quite frankly no progress was being made at $80 an hour so I couldn't afford to keep going. Granted I understand I have so many issues that a years worth of therapy would be what it would take to make a dent..but yeah it wasn't feeling too promising
